recipes.name: Fried Pickles
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste
1 teaspoon seafood seasoning, such as Old Bay™

steps.text: Line a plate with parchment paper or wax paper; set aside. Combine buttermilk, salt, and black pepper in a shallow dish. Add pickles; set aside.

Place cornmeal, flour, seafood seasoning, and ¼ teaspoon Cajun seasoning in a large, resealable plastic bag; shake to combine. Add pickles, a few at a time, and shake gently to evenly coat with cornmeal mixture. Remove pickles; place on the prepared plate.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy deep skillet to 365 degrees F (180 degrees C).

Lower pickles carefully into the hot oil in batches. Fry until golden brown and slightly crisp on the outside with a moist interior, 1 to 2 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Repeat with remaining pickles.
Combine buttermilk ranch dressing and remaining ½ teaspoon Cajun seasoning in a small bowl. Serve as a dipping sauce for warm fried pickles.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Pickles
raw_recipe.description: This fried pickles recipe starts with a buttermilk marinade and cornmeal coating. Old Bay and Cajun seasonings spice up the coating and ranch dressing.

review.reviewBody: Awesome recipe. I did not use the seafood seasoning because I did not have it. But I did use the Cajun and it was good. It tasted just like eating out. Also, I picked this recipe because it did not have eggs. I was beginning to think you could not fry pickles without eggs. Thanks so much poster.

This recipe nails it. I added more Old Bay because I am from Baltimore and that's just what we do. The ranch side with the cajun seasoning is perfect. I actually think this recipe works better with the pickle spears. Really make sure you coat them with the batter, otherwise the fried layer is too thin.

Awesome breading that I can see being very versatile. Super easy to prepare. I did not have buttermilk but really wanted some fried pickles so I took them straight from the jar into the breading and fired them. They were perfect. Just what I was in the mood for. My kids even said they were better than some popular restaurant fried pickles they have had. I made a whole 32 ounce jar of hamburger dills with just one recipe of this amazing breading!
Wow. This turned out great. The one and only change I made was that I used whole pickles and cut them myself a bit thicker than normal sliced dill pickles. Turned out excellent.
I didn't have buttermilk so used whole milk and a tsp of lemon. My husband thought this was the best Fried dill pickles recipe so far! We are on #4 now.
Delish! I used mini dills instead of slices and I dipped them twice in the breading (with buttermilk in between) for a really crunchy exterior. Thanks!

These are good, but here is how to make them even better. And easier too! 
Forget about dipping and dredging. Make a semi-thick batter with ingredients. Dip the drained pickles into the batter and fry. So much easier and with much better results. And use the crispiest thickest chips you can find.

These were so good. We are a gluten free family so we used our normal gluten free flour blend in place of the AP Flour and it worked wonderfully. Crispy yummy fried pickles. Thanks so much for sharing!
Update- I just realized that I didn't even notice last time that there was more cornmeal than flour so I used 3/4 c flour and 3/4 cornmeal, and you won't be disappointed. Whatever amount you use, just use equal parts flour and cornmeal.

My sweet baby girl grand daughter requested fried pickles for Thanksgiving. Tested some small batches and this is the recipe we liked best. Super crust, super easy. One change, I didn't have Cajun seasoning (on my shopping list) so I used soul seasoning and I had to add some cayenne to give it a little more punch.

I typically don't like fried pickles but for some reason had a craving. So, I went on the hunt for the best recipe I could find. This one is it! I changed up the seasoning a little bit because I don't like cajun spicy stuff. Added some garlic and paprika and they turned out so delicious! I'll definitely be making these again very soon!

I thought this was delicious. I didnt have any cornmeal so I used some bread cumbs (a little less than amount of flour used) and I added a splash of cayenne pepper, and a little paprika. I also used garlic oil. I made other recipies on this site using the egg and ect, and thought this recipie was much tastier and easier to make. I havent got to the making a dipping sauce yet cause I didnt need one. great recipie, this one makes the recipie book. :)
So good! My favorite fried pickle recipe by far
Home run! By far the best fried pickles I have attempted to make.
THE BEST!!! These are the best I've ever had!!! Better than anything from a restaurant, from the store, whatever! THANK YOU, Mama Smith!!!!
first time making them and everyone loved them. That's why I didn't get a picture. Definitely save this one
We all loved these. I wasn't shy with the spices.

THIS IS AMAZING!!! Restaurant quality fried pickles!! I added a little more of the seasoning than in the recipe so I encourage others to play around with it. I was worried the breading wouldn’t stick but it did great! Very crunchy and delicious!

These were great! Everyone in the house ate them up! My kids usually don’t like fried pickles but devoured these. I omitted the seafood seasoning but kept the rest the same. Will definitely make these again!
I have made this a few times. It’s definitely a keeper !
No changes were made, I'd definitely make it again!
